name: Fasnachtshaus Nassereith
kurzbeschreibung: The Nassereith Carnival House: award-winning traditional museum for the Schellerlaufen with over 400 artistic wooden masks by master carvers.
beschreibung:
Overview

The award-winning Nassereith Carnival House is located on the picturesque Postplatz in the heart of the Tyrolean Oberland municipality of Nassereith (Imst district) at an altitude of around 840 meters above sea level. Situated directly at the entrance to the Gurgltal valley and on the historic Fernpass route, this modern special museum is entirely dedicated to the Nassereith Schellerlaufen. This centuries-old carnival custom is one of the most colorful, expressive, and significant traditional events in the entire Alpine region and has been officially included in the UNESCO Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Austria.

Route & Requirements

The Nassereith Schellerlaufen takes place every three years according to tradition and captivates tens of thousands of visitors. The Carnival House was opened in 2008 to make the fascination of this ancient fertility and winter expulsion custom tangible throughout the year. The centerpiece of the exhibition is the world's largest and most significant collection of over 400 hand-carved wooden masks (Larven) from three centuries. Nassereith is famous for its unique carving tradition: artists like Franz Josef Falger created masks of unsurpassed plasticity and masterful emotional expression in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Visit & Arrival

The Nassereith Carnival House is open from May to the end of October on Fridays and Sundays from 15:00 to 18:00 (extended opening hours in winter during carnival season; for groups of 8 or more, open year-round by prior arrangement). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €14.00. Holders of the regional Urlaubspass Imst receive discounted admission. Arrival by car: Via the Fernpassstraße B179 or B189 directly to Nassereith; parking is available at Postplatz or the community center (free). By public transport: ÖBB to Imst-Pitztal train station, from there VVT bus line 4206 runs every half hour directly to the Nassereith Postplatz stop (only a one-minute walk to the museum).

Tips

The Carnival House is excellently barrier-free and wheelchair accessible; all floors are easily reached by a modern passenger elevator. Take your time for the film screening in the in-house cinema to experience the archaic energy of the Schellerlaufen up close. After your visit, take a stroll to the idyllic Nassereith Lake at the foot of the rock face, which is only about a five-minute walk away, and deepen the fascinating insights into the vibrant, traditional Tyrolean customs for history and culture-minded guests of all ages.
